questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That I could go with my two friends, that is seemed like a nice city and that it was in Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not too easy, but I had two friends with me, so we could help each other.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We received help from the mobility coordinator from Vienna University.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think it was a good orientation, but there was still a lot to figure out yourself.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I googled it, and found a dormitory. It wasn't very hard.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I lived in a house under the Öjab housing, and it was pretty good. A bit dirty and not so social for Danish standards, but cheap, good location, pretty good room and I had my own bathroom which was really nice.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: We had to show up to and orientation, which was short and sweet. I found it very difficult to find courses in English within my own field of study (sociology), but ended up finding some courses in STS and Anthropology. But it was very difficult making it match the 30 ECTS that was required from UCPH in English and Master levels, but I managed in collaboration with my two friends who took the same courses. This also made making the Online Learning Agreement quite complicated, as the deadlines for this and the deadlines for when we knew if we were admitted to the courses we wanted didn't match.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: We asked our mobility coordinator and she was helpful to a certain degree.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I took all the course I thought I could get, and got into enough to reach 30 ECTS.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Maybe start out in good time, and trust that it will be alright.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the level of the courses were fine. It was clear that it was masters level though, and as I had to have 7 courses to reach 30 ECTS it was quite a big workload. I had many courses outside of my own field of study, so some of it was quite. confusing to me, but still very manageable.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There wasn't as many lecture were you only had to listen, but much more participation and you also got points for participation, which I found very different from Copenhagen. In my courses you pretty much just had to show up to get the participation points though, and do a bit of presentations, so it was fine. A lot more group work and talking to the people in the class, but it differed quite a lot from course to course. The have different types of courses, so you can choose what type of teaching you like. I had one reading seminar, where we discussed texts, and there was little lecturing from the teacher, and I (surprisingly) really liked that course.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Imagining Mobility, 
Popular culture and digital visyality, 
Writing and representing in STS, 
What is Power? (reading seminar), 
Political Sociology, 
Urban Sociology, 
STS Borders and Mobility,

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Really depends on what your interested in. 
Can't recommend Urban Sociology, as I didn't like the lectures at all. 
Can recommend: What is Power, STS Borders and Mobility, Political Sociology.

questions.answer: drinks were cheap, and i didn't have to buy any books.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Didn't find or participate in any.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't really think there were any, but I didn't look into it either.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Can't say.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out and eat cake and drink cofeee. And drink Spritzers. There are A LOT of things going on in the city, also for free, so look into that. Go to Kahleenberg for a good view over the city, or drink spritzers or go to the open air cinema on top of the stairs of the public library. Otherwise just enjoy the city, it is soooo beautiful.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Didn't manage, other than the people who lived in the same dorm as me, but they were also mostly not from Vienna. Met some people going out, that we hung out with.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There was a lot of paperwork and bureaucracy in regards to registration, but otherwise nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The coffee culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be sure to enjoy the city while you are there, and remember to not use all your time studying. 
Find some people to share your experiences with.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
It can seem like there is a lot of registration things that you have to do, but as long as you stay on top of it, you will be fine. 
Also I got a Swapfiets bike, which was very nice and pretty cheap, but the public transportation was also pretty good if your not much of a biker.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in such a beautiful city with some of my best friends.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All of the registrations both at uni and at the municipality office.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
